NINE HOLE GOLF — KEYS AND TIMING

We checked the BASIC program and played two club selections in Fuse 1.6.0 on the 48K machine.

The original tape starts the first hole without a separate menu. It draws the golfer, flag, bunkers, and distance to the hole. At the prompt, enter a club number from 1 through 8 and press Enter. The BASIC reads that number to choose a swing. We pressed 1, saw an overshot notice, and then pressed 8 on the next displayed course. The replay also saves the starting screen so the first move can be checked. Hole positions are randomized; we do not claim a completed round.

From the repository root, run:
  sh src/assets/basic-src/original-sinclair-basic-collections/Granada-Publishing/13-nine-hole-golf/BASIC/REPLAY.sh

Fuse runs at 100% speed. Waits are in real seconds.

  1. Open the original TAP with the 48K ROM. Wait 3 seconds and save 00-START.png.
  2. Enter 1 and press Enter. Wait 5 seconds and save 01-AFTER-CLUB-1.png.
  3. Enter 8 and press Enter. Wait 6 seconds and save 02-AFTER-CLUB-8.png.

The replay compares the course area before and after both inputs. The captures show a short play sample, not a full round.
